short: ConvLSTM top layer (M06) is standard: new to ultrasound-to-speech, but a 2.1% MSE edge over BiLSTM from one speaker and one run; later work dropped it. MSE-only evaluation (M12 behind).
position: The paper [@shandiz2022improved] changes one component (M06): a unidirectional ConvLSTM replaces the top layers of its group's 3D-CNN ultrasound front end, and test MSE on 80 standardized mel targets falls from 0.293 (3D-CNN) and 0.282 (3D-CNN + BiLSTM) to 0.276, 5.8% and 2.1% relative (inference). M06 is standard: the layer is new to ultrasound-to-speech mapping (9 ConvLSTM pattern matches among 148 ultrasound studies, none an earlier speech-output study; Appendix), but the edge over the BiLSTM is one run on one speaker, with dropout and pooling changed alongside (Table 1). The design did not carry forward: the group returned to the plain 3D-CNN in 2023 [@toth2023adaptation], and the 2026 state of the art, a 3D front end with a Transformer, tests no ConvLSTM [@sonkar2026tongue2speech]. Evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work: MSE and mean R² only, although the same mel-plus-WaveGlow pipeline had gone through a MUSHRA test in 2020 [@csapo2020waveglow]. The "smaller and faster" claim (Abstract) has no measurement behind it.
